request.spec:
When a claim is opened it receives the next number on the sheet: 1 for the first claim ever
opened on the sheet, then 2, and so on, with no gaps and never reused, even when two users open
claims at the same moment. A draft has no number, and voiding a claim clears its number (the
number is not given to anyone else). Show the number on the claim. Every audit line about a
claim that has a number gains number=<number> at its end (so CLAIM_OPENED and CLAIM_SETTLED
carry it; a CLAIM_VOIDED line carries the number the claim had).

When a claim is opened it receives the next number on the sheet: 1 for the first claim ever

claims at the same moment. A draft has no number, and voiding a claim clears its number (the

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claim numbering is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the acceptance spec, including the one where two users open claims at the same moment.

**How it works:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V8__claim_number.sql`, adds a counter to each sheet (`sheet.claim_number`, the last number given out) and a nullable `claim_no` column on `claim`.
- **Opening a claim:** the server first moves the claim from draft to open, and only if that succeeds does it add one to the sheet's counter and give the new value to the claim (`ClaimRepository.number`). A refused open never touches the counter, so there are no gaps. The whole thing runs in one transaction, and the sheet's row stays locked until it commits, so two claims opened at once get one number each, in sequence.
- **Voiding a claim:** the number is cleared and the counter is left alone, so that number is never given to another claim. The `CLAIM_VOIDED` line still carries the number the claim had, and a voided draft has no number to carry.
- **Audit lines:** `number=<n>` goes at the end of `CLAIM_OPENED` and `CLAIM_SETTLED`, and of `CLAIM_VOIDED` when the claim had a number.
- **Screen:** each claim row now has a `claim-number` cell, which is empty for drafts and voided claims.

Two choices of mine you may want to know about:
- `CLAIM_EDITED` also gets `number=<n>` when the edited claim has a number. The request said every audit line about a numbered claim should carry it. The test only edits drafts, so nothing checks this.
- I named the claim's column `claim_no` rather than `number`, because `NUMBER` is an SQL type keyword in H2.
